observations.why: The 'we' framing enacts communal-sharing — a collective decision presented as shared identity, not individual command.
Proportionality framing — quantified benefit and cost reduction cast the switch as a cost/benefit calculus, the hallmark of market-pricing.
The arrow notation frames the migration as a substitution transaction — one resource replaced by another on cost/benefit grounds, continuing the market-pricing frame from src-2.
Quantified performance gain restates the proportionality calculus — benefit measured in multiples, the market-pricing register.
Setting a timeline enacts authority-ranking — a schedule imposed as a directive, allocating time as a rank-based resource.
